{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Charles Waldo Rezk''' (born 26 January 1969) is an American mathematician, specializing in [[algebraic topology]] and [[category theory]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Charles Rezk's homepage|website=Department of Mathematics, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|url=https://rezk.web.illinois.edu/}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Rezk matriculated at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in 1987 and graduated there in 1991 with B.A. and M.A. in mathematics.<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=Charles W. Rezk, Curriculum Vitae|website=Department of Mathematics, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|url=https://rezk.web.illinois.edu/cv-rezk-2024.pdf}}</ref> In 1996 he received his PhD from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] with thesis ''Spaces of Algebra Structures and Cohomology of Operads'' and advisor [[Michael J. Hopkins]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=37595|title=Charles Waldo Rezk}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Rezk, C. W.|date=May 1996|title=Spaces of algebra structures and cohomology of operads (Doctoral dissertation, Massachusetts Institute of Technology)|website=dspace.mit.edu|url=https://dspace.mit.edu/bitstream/handle/1721.1/41793/36023226-MIT.pdf?sequence=2}}</ref> At [[Northwestern University]] Rezk was a faculty member from 1996 to 2001. At the [[University of Illinois]] he was an assistant professor from 2001 to 2006 and an associate professor from 2006 to 2014, and has been a full professor since 2014.<ref name=CV/>

He was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in the fall of 1999, the spring of 2000, and the spring of 2001.<ref>{{cite web|title=Charles Rezk|website=Institute for Advanced Study|date=9 December 2019 |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/charles-rezk}}</ref> He held visiting positions at MIT in 2006 and at Berkeley's [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]] in 2014. Since 2015 he has been a member of the editorial board of ''[[Compositio Mathematica]]''.<ref name=CV/>

Rezk was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Seoul in 2014.<ref>{{cite book|author=Rezk, Charles|chapter=Isogenies, power operations, and homotopy theory|title=Proceedings of the ICM, Seoul|volume=2|year=2014|pages=1125–1146|chapter-url=https://rezk.web.illinois.edu/rezk-icm-talk-posted.pdf}} [https://rezk.web.illinois.edu/rezk-icm-2014-handout.pdf slides]</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in the class of 2015 (announced in late 2014).<ref name=CV/>

The [[Ando–Hopkins–Rezk orientation]] is named after him.
